episode_title: The Visibility Playbook for Internal Comms w/ Dave Cordero

real_qa.q: How did the PGA Tour build internal communications from zero when Dave Cordero joined in 2017?
real_qa.r: Cordero conducted a three-month listening tour to meet with department leaders and understand their expectations. He found the organization of 1,400 employees was still behaving as a small company with excessive email noise including reply-alls and disjointed messaging. He implemented an editorial calendar requiring email approval, then developed a biweekly newsletter sent every Tuesday at 2 p.m. to consolidate communications and reduce noise.
real_qa.requete: PGA Tour internal communications built from scratch 2017

real_qa.q: What metrics did the PGA Tour implement to measure internal communications visibility?
real_qa.r: After discovering their CEO's video message via Dropbox had no view tracking capability, the PGA Tour adopted Banana Tag (later acquired by StaffBase) which allowed tracking of open rates, read time buckets (eight seconds or more, skimmed, glanced), and link clicks. This provided visibility into which content resonated with employees and became their first major moment to demonstrate communications effectiveness to executives.
real_qa.requete: StaffBase Banana Tag internal comms metrics tracking

real_qa.q: How should organizations approach rolling out WorkVivo or major internal communications platforms?
real_qa.r: Dave Cordero recommends testing with a pilot group first before full launch, ensuring the platform is fully functional, building executive sponsorship, and using multi-channel promotion including digital signage and newsletters. After witnessing a failed wellness benefits launch that was deployed too early with bugs and no promotion, he emphasized not pulling back the curtain until everything is ready and using ambassadors to build adoption gradually.
real_qa.requete: WorkVivo launch strategy internal communications adoption

real_qa.q: What is the People Leader Report and how does it solve internal communications challenges at the PGA Tour?
real_qa.r: The People Leader Report is a newsletter sent to approximately 300 managers at the PGA Tour that provides three to five key points they need to know and share with their teams each week. It cascades critical information from compliance requirements to town hall announcements, ensuring managers have the information to cascade down and eliminating knowledge gaps where employees might hear news from external sources before internal channels.
real_qa.requete: People Leader Report newsletter manager communications

real_qa.q: What were the top three employee concerns revealed in the PGA Tour's recent employee engagement survey?
real_qa.r: The survey revealed three main themes: communications (employees reported never knowing what is going on and learning about company news on social media or Instagram before internal channels), career development (employees wanting to know how to advance), and belonging and inclusion. Remote employees were notably the loudest on communication concerns, leading to the creation of the People Leader Report and external weekly email snapshot.
real_qa.requete: PGA Tour employee engagement survey communications findings

real_qa.q: How did the PGA Tour address employee uncertainty about company news affecting their personal lives?
real_qa.r: Cordero and his communications department created a weekly email sent Monday afternoons providing a snapshot of external news, message points, and the PGA Tour's position on various topics. Employees previously reported being afraid to attend family gatherings or speak with neighbors without knowing what was happening publicly, so this document allowed them to quickly skim critical information and become informed ambassadors.
real_qa.requete: external news snapshot employee awareness communications

guest.bio_context: Dave majored in public relations from a school of journalism in Southern California. He spent approximately 20 years in external communications including media relations and work for sports teams, then worked in-house for a golf company before joining the PGA Tour in 2017, where he was tasked with building the internal communications function from the ground up.
